label: q input at step 4-5 of a sequence starting with a
explanation: Very sparse feature, active only during the original phase. It fires when the input is q (86% of activation mass) at original position 4-5 (95% of mass) in sequences whose first token is a (98% of mass). It is strongest when the intervening tokens include 1/2/3, k, p, h or t; the top examples are a 1 k p q, a 1 2 p q and a 1 3 3 q. Even so, most a...q at step 4-5 occurrences do not activate it (precision about 0.26), so the exact history dependence is only partly captured. It never fires in the copy phase, at t<3 or at t>6, and rarely on non-q inputs (these are weak activations on letters such as v, w, u right after an a-1-..-p-like prefix).
